messages:
Maddie Li: Heads-up — hit a corner case when a user-agent route and auth-header override both exist. Some requests are landing on the wrong model variant because the auth proxy rewrites X-Route after routing already happened. :thinking:
Samir Patel: Oof. Are we doing header-based route selection before or after auth enrichment? That ordering matters a lot for precedence.
Jorge R.: Currently the gateway runs matchers in this order: path -> host -> header-match. Auth enrichment (adds X-User, X-Tenant) happens in a later filter. So if a client sets `User-Agent: Redwood-A/Beta` we route to beta variant, but if auth proxy rewrites `X-Route` later it can change which backend is chosen in internal metadata — confusing.
Priya Nair: We should decide: do we let external headers (User-Agent, X-Custom-Route) directly control routing, or should authenticated context (derived headers) be authoritative for tenancy/quotas? Two different concerns.
Maddie Li: My proposal: split concerns. Routing selectors (which model variant/service to use) should be computed from original incoming headers + path/host at match-time. Auth-derived headers should be used for identity/authorization/quota attribution only and not mutate the routing decision unless explicitly allowed by a route policy.
Samir Patel: I like that. So default = external headers control route selection, auth headers control quota/tenant. And add an explicit `allow_auth_override: true` flag on routes if we want auth to override routing.
Jorge R.: Agreed. Also need to handle SDK user-agent churn — many SDKs set `User-Agent` with version. We have to support prefix matching (`User-Agent: Redwood-SDK/*`) and a lower precedence than an exact `X-Redwood-Route` header.
Priya Nair: UX: console should show an indicator on the route config — "Header-based routing precedence: exact > prefix > regex > auth-override" and a toggle for `Allow auth header override` with a tooltip explaining risks.
Maddie Li: Example gateway policy snippet to illustrate:```yaml
- match:
    headers:
      X-Redwood-Route: { exact: "model-beta" }
      User-Agent: { prefix: "Redwood-SDK" }
  route:
    backend: inference-beta
  allow_auth_override: false
```
Samir Patel: Good. We should also log which selector picked the route for telemetry: add `route_selector` tag with values like `header:X-Redwood-Route`, `ua-prefix`, `path`, `auth-override` so we can break down latency/cost attribution.
Jorge R.: Also, security: mask PII in any header we log (X-Forwarded-User can contain emails). We should only log hashed or truncated values and keep a flag `log_raw_headers: false` by default.
Priya Nair: On quotas: enforcement should reference the auth-derived tenant header (X-Tenant-ID) even if route was chosen by user-agent. Otherwise a malicious client could bypass tenant limits by hitting a different route.
Maddie Li: Right — routing and quota identity must be decoupled. Route determines code path + model, auth header determines billing/quota/telemetry identity.
Samir Patel: Edge-case: health checks and retries. Health-checks lack auth headers; ensure they match default route or a dedicated health route. Also on retry, don't allow auth proxy to flip route mid-flight — immutable per-request route decision.
Jorge R.: Implementation plan: (1) compute route_key from original request headers/path/host; (2) run matchers and select backend; (3) enrich request with auth headers; (4) apply quotas and attribution using enriched headers; (5) if route has `allow_auth_override` then re-evaluate matchers with auth headers and allow explicit override with audit log.
Priya Nair: Can infra-bot emit a config check that warns if you enable `allow_auth_override` for public routes? We should require an explicit risk ack for exposed routes.
infra-bot: Added: config-lint rule `no-public-auth-overrides` (warn) and `require-ack-for-auth-override` (soft-error).
Maddie Li: Perfect. Last thing — update console metrics: show a small badge on routes indicating how many requests were matched by `user-agent` vs `auth-override` in the last 24h, and add a saved filter `route_selector:auth-override` for ops.
Samir Patel: I'll open a PR with code + unit tests for precedence, and a follow-up PR for console UX.
Maddie Li: Thanks — assign to me for review. :thumbsup:
